record.final_answer:
Four SKUs need reordering:

| SKU | Stock (all warehouses) | Reorder level |
|---|---|---|
| BX-100 | 23 | 25 |
| CL-310 | 5 | 5 (at level) |
| EN-512 | 0 | 10 |
| GH-118 | 7 | 12 |

BX-220 (40 against 30), DR-045 (120 against 80) and FT-760 (33 against 20) are above their levels. Every SKU in `reorder.csv` appears in the export.

The plain command `python3 restock.py exports/stock-2026-10-27.csv` failed with "column 'sku' not found". The supplier portal starts the file with a UTF-8 byte-order mark, an invisible marker that got stuck to the first column name. The script already has an `--encoding` option, so I ran it with `--encoding utf-8-sig`, which reads past that marker. I didn't change the export or `restock.py`.

Future exports from the portal will probably need `--encoding utf-8-sig` too. I saved this to memory so later sessions know about it.
